data.narrative:
Floodbase, a Series A climate and energy company founded by Bessie Schwarz and Dr. Beth Tellman, has raised $17M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a sector peer universe comprising 1 public comparable (LNZA) and 8 private companies including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Only one valuation method proved applicable. The stage-progression approach uses the $17M raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression, yielding $34M. A peer-median analysis was not feasible; while 8 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, none met the narrow filters for stage alignment or valuation tier similarity required for meaningful triangulation, and an all-sector median would introduce excessive noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $29M to $39M, with a median of $34M. This range reflects primarily the stage-progression method's output, with the bounds capturing reasonable variance around that central estimate. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-cohort peer comparables, limiting cross-validation of the step-up multiplier, and the nascent maturity of climate-tech valuations broadly. The valuation assumes continued capital availability and execution consistent with Series A milestone expectations in the frontier-technology segment.
